characteristics_interventions.S:
(1) High-intensity task-oriented training

"The high-intensity task-oriented training-programme incorporated 10 standardized work-stations, focused on improving walking competency, similar to the study by Deanet al. (19). Participants in the high-intensity training-group performed 45 minutes of circuit class training, held at the rehabilitation clinic three times a week for four weeks. All stations were practised for 2.5 minutes, followed by a 1-minute transfer to the next station. Afterwards the participants joined in walking relays and races for 10 minutes.The high-intensity training-programme focused on improving postural control and gait-related activities such as stair walking, turning, making transfers, walking quickly and walking for specified distances. In line with the recommendations of the American Heart Association, (22) cardiorespiratory workload started at 40–50% of heart rate reserve. Progression was attained by increasing the worknload to a maximum of 70–80% of heart rate reserve, (25), and increasing the number of repetitions, both according to the observations and estimation of the therapists in charge and the patient's perceived exertion. A 6–20 Borg Scale was used to rate subjects’ perceived exertion"

(2) Low-intensity physiotherapy

"The focus in the low-intensity physiotherapy-group was on improving motor control of the hemiparetic leg and balance. In contrast to the high-intensity training group there were no components of physical fitness training such as strengthen-ing exercises or cardiorespiratory training, indicating that the training was set at a low-intensity profile aimed at learning gait-related activities. The participants in the low-intensity physiotherapy group went through a 45-minute programme of group exercises, three times a week for four weeks, thus matching therapy time to the high-intensity training-group. The low-intensity physiotherapy-programme was also based on a 10 work stations circuit. All stations were practised for 2.5 minutes, followed by a 1-minute gap to transfer to the next station. Afterwards the participants joined in games, like passing through a ball, for 10 minutes. Progression, according to the observations and estimation of the therapists in charge, was achieved by enhancing motor control challenge, not in enhancing the number of repetitions like the high-intensity training-group."

"All participants engaged in usual individual physiotherapy for half an hour each day. Information about intensity and content of the therapy beyond the trial were documented in a patient’s record. Therapists were instructed not to depart from their usual care during the trial."

# YYYMethods

Study aim: to investigate the feasibility and the effects on gait of a high intensity task-oriented training, incorporating a high cardiovascular workload and large number of repetitions, in patients with subacute stroke, when compared to a low-intensity physiotherapy-programme

Design: parallel-group RCT

Country: Netherlands

Study recruitment and setting: see Table 7

Involvement of patients/public/professionals/others: no

# YYYParticipants

Study population (number randomised): 44

Inclusion criteria:

- Diagnosis of hemiplegia following first or recurrent stroke

- 2 to 8 weeks since most recent stroke and recruitment

- Able to walk 10 m without assistance

- FAC ≥ 3

Exclusion criteria:

- Cardiovascular instability

- Acute impairment of lower extremities influencing walking

- Sensory communicative disorders

Participants: detailed in Table 28

PROGRESS-plus: summarised in Table 10

# YYYInterventions

(1) High-intensity task-oriented training

"The high-intensity task-oriented training-programme incorporated 10 standardized work-stations, focused on improving walking competency, similar to the study by Deanet al. (19). Participants in the high-intensity training-group performed 45 minutes of circuit class training, held at the rehabilitation clinic three times a week for four weeks. All stations were practised for 2.5 minutes, followed by a 1-minute transfer to the next station. Afterwards the participants joined in walking relays and races for 10 minutes.The high-intensity training-programme focused on improving postural control and gait-related activities such as stair walking, turning, making transfers, walking quickly and walking for specified distances. In line with the recommendations of the American Heart Association, (22) cardiorespiratory workload started at 40–50% of heart rate reserve. Progression was attained by increasing the worknload to a maximum of 70–80% of heart rate reserve, (25), and increasing the number of repetitions, both according to the observations and estimation of the therapists in charge and the patient's perceived exertion. A 6–20 Borg Scale was used to rate subjects’ perceived exertion"

(2) Low-intensity physiotherapy

"The focus in the low-intensity physiotherapy-group was on improving motor control of the hemiparetic leg and balance. In contrast to the high-intensity training group there were no components of physical fitness training such as strengthen-ing exercises or cardiorespiratory training, indicating that the training was set at a low-intensity profile aimed at learning gait-related activities. The participants in the low-intensity physiotherapy group went through a 45-minute programme of group exercises, three times a week for four weeks, thus matching therapy time to the high-intensity training-group. The low-intensity physiotherapy-programme was also based on a 10 work stations circuit. All stations were practised for 2.5 minutes, followed by a 1-minute gap to transfer to the next station. Afterwards the participants joined in games, like passing through a ball, for 10 minutes. Progression, according to the observations and estimation of the therapists in charge, was achieved by enhancing motor control challenge, not in enhancing the number of repetitions like the high-intensity training-group."

"All participants engaged in usual individual physiotherapy for half an hour each day. Information about intensity and content of the therapy beyond the trial were documented in a patient’s record. Therapists were instructed not to depart from their usual care during the trial."

| Bias domain                                                                     | Authors’ judgement | Support for judgement                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Random sequence generation (selection bias)**                                 | Low risk           | Random sequence generated using a computer random number generator.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| **Allocation concealment (selection bias)**                                     | Low risk           | Randomisation schedule held by a research pharmacist not involved in other aspects of the study. The code for participant assignment was held by the research pharmacy until completion of data analysis.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| **Blinding of participants and personnel (performance bias): All outcomes**     | Low risk           | Both participants and research staff were blinded, equivalent active and placebo pills were ingested, and blinding success tests were performed at trial exit, indicating successful blinding.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| **Blinding of outcome assessment (detection bias): Self-reported outcomes**     | Low risk           | Participants were blinded, and a blinding success test was performed at trial exit, indicating successful blinding.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| **Blinding of outcome assessment (detection bias): Assessor-reported outcomes** | Low risk           | No assessor-reported outcomes of interest to this review.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| **Incomplete outcome data (attrition bias)**                                    | High risk          | 38/121 (31%) of participants withdrew from the trial; number of withdrawals that continued to provide outcome data was not reported. While all 121 randomised participants were included in ITT analysis, last-observation-carried-forward was used as the method of imputation. * 21 to 65 years of age
* low back pain (T-6 or below, secondary to degenerative disc disease) present “on a daily basis” for the previous 6 months or longer
* English speaking, literate, and able to understand and communicate with the study team
* not a present candidate for back surgery
* CYP-450 2D6 extensive metabolizer phenotype

## Exclusion criteria

* major coexisting medical illness which might confound assessment of function or life quality or other conditions for which classical antidepressants would be inappropriate
* another coexisting chronic pain problem
* significant coexisting musculoskeletal disorder, sciatica as a primary problem, or back pain due to systemic disorders
* history within the previous 12 months of alcohol or other substance-use disorder, major depression, or dysthymia
* lifetime history of bipolar disorder or psychosis
* dementia
* known allergy to the study drugs
* use of psychoactive agents that would need to be continued during the study, or other agents that might interact with the study drugs before treatment with study agents
* CYP-450 2D6 poor metabolizer phenotype

# YYYMethods

* Study design: parallel-group RCT

* Study centre: multi-centre (5 study centers from 4 tertiary hospitals in China)

* Number randomised: 264 children

* Study follow-up: 12 months

* Exclusions and losses to follow-up: 18 (6.8%) children who were randomised were excluded or lost to follow-up (2 in the red light therapy group and 16 in the SVL group)

# YYYParticipants

* Age: median = 10.4 years (range 8.0 to 13.0 years) in red light therapy group, 10.5 (range 8.1 to 13.0) in SVL group

* Gender: 130 boys, 134 girls

* Culture: Chinese

* Inclusion criteria:

* age 8-13 years
* myopia with SER between −1.00 D and −5.00 D by cycloplegic refraction
* astigmatism of 2.50 D or less
* anisometropia of 1.50 D or less
* BCVA LogMAR 0.0 or better
* Exclusion criteria:

* strabismus, binocular vision abnormalities in either eye
* systemic disease
* previous myopia control treatment

# YYYInterventions

* Low level red light therapy (n = 119): desktop device delivering red light with a wavelength 650nm at illumination level 1600 lux (3 minutes per session, 2 sessions per weekday, with a minimum 4-hour interval)

* SVL (n = 145): single vision spectacle lenses

* Primary outcome

* Change in AL from baseline
* Secondary outcomes

* Change in SER from baseline
* Visual acuity
* Anterior chamber depth
* Corneal curvature
* Corneal diameter
* Measurements taken at baseline and 1, 3, 6 and 12 months

* Unit of analysis child level (right eyes)

characteristics_interventions.S:
**Intervention**

System-wide operational initiatives and protocols were developed and implemented in 2010. A single North Ohio Trauma System (NOTS) transfer line was created and housed in the L1TC to coordinate hospital transfers. A non-trauma hospital transfer/triage protocol was implemented according to patients' physiologic, anatomic, and mechanistic parameters. Shortly after, scene triage protocols were well implemented. Various NOTS committees were convened on a monthly basis, they included quality, protocol development, prevention, compliance, and network. In addition, a dedicated trauma intensive care unit (TICU), staffed by trauma/critical care attending physicians, was established at NOTS L1TC.

**Description of rationale, theory, or goal of essential elements to the intervention**

Traditional trauma systems were composed of single hospital systems that focused on the local need for trauma care. These systems failed to allocate resources based on patients' medical needs appropriately. A more recently inclusive regional trauma system incorporated medical centres within a geographical area with a hierarchical trauma level designation. Multiple studies performed outside the United States have shown that inclusive regional trauma systems can improve clinical and functional outcomes of adult and pediatric patients. Contrastingly, there was a scarcity of studies investigating the impact of these systems in the United States.

**Description of providers (background, expertise, training)**

The trauma departments and critical care units at level 1 trauma centres were staffed by trauma-trained physicians and critical-care providers.

**Mode of delivery of the intervention (face-to-face, by telephone, Internet)**

Direct clinical care.

**Description of location(s) infrastructure or relevant features of where intervention occurred**

The trauma network includes 2 level 1 and 4 level 2 trauma centres and seven non-trauma hospitals. In addition, a pre-hospital retrieval and treatment system coordinated by the level 1 trauma centres in North Ohio.

**How well was their intervention planned (if they assessed fidelity or adherence, describe how, by who, and if they employed strategies for maintaining fidelity)**

Limited descriptions of the physical infrastructure and how the intervention was implemented.

**How well was the intervention carried out, description of how the intervention adhered to the plan**

Not described.

**Intervention**

# YYYOutcomes

Two analyses were done for the post-NOTS period:

1. A county analysis, comparing Cuyahoga County, the county containing NOTS L1TC, with other counties containing L1TCs.
2. A regional analysis, comparing the NOTS region with other Ohio regions with L1TC coverage.

Both the county and regional analyses showed the overall NOTS patients were 1 to 4 years older (p < 0.05), had similar or higher Injury Severity Score (p < 0.05), and were treated more often at lower-level TCs (p < 0.001). County analysis demonstrated that Cuyahoga County had approximately 1% lower mortality in geriatrics patients than non-NOTS counties. Regional analysis showed lower mortality in the NOTS region for the overall patient group and geriatric and blunt injuries subgroups. Cuyahoga was the only county that decreased mortality for both the general and groups over time (all p < 0.05).

* Study design: paired-eye, cross-over RCT

* Study centre: single (Department of Optometry, University of Auckland)

* Number randomised: 40 children

* Study follow-up: 20 months (10 months for each period)

* Exclusions and losses to follow-up: no exclusions; 5 (12.5%) and 6 (15.0%) were lost to follow-up at 10-month visit and 20-month visit, respectively

# YYYParticipants

* Age: mean = 13.4 years (range 11-14 years)

* Gender: 11 boys, 29 girls

* Culture: New Zealand, including East Asian ethnicity and others (European, Indian, and Maori/Pacifica)

* Inclusion criteria:

* 11-14 years old at recruitment
* spherical equivalent between −1.25 and −4.50 D in the least myopic eye as determined by noncycloplegic subjective refraction
* myopia progression ≥ 0.50 D in the previous 12 months
* best-corrected spectacle VA of Snellen 6/6 or better in each eye
* willingness to wear contact lenses for ≥ 8 h/day during the study
* Exclusion criteria: history of

* astigmatism ≥ 1.25 D
* anisometropia ≥ 1.00 D
* strabismus at distance or near as assessed by cover test
* ocular or systemic pathology likely to affect refractive development or successful contact lens wear
* birth weight ≤ 1250 g

# YYYInterventions

* Group 1 (n = 21): 10 months wearing 2.00 D DF contact lens in the dominant eye and SVSCL in the contralateral eye, followed by 10 months wearing the swapped lens assignment

* Group 2 (n = 19): 10 months wearing DF contact lens in the nondominant eye and SVSCL in the contralateral eye, followed by 10 months wearing the swapped lens assignment

# YYYOutcomes

* Primary outcome:

* Change in spherical equivalent refraction measured by cycloplegic autorefraction
* Secondary outcome:

* Change in AL measured by partial coherence interferometry
* Measurements taken at baseline and every 5 months for 20 months

* Unit of analysis: data analysed by dominant eye

* **Country:** France.

* Participants had AD or mixed dementia according to DSM-IV criteria.
* **Inclusion criterion:** MMSE ≤ 20.
* **Exclusion criterion:** High musical expertise as assessed by the Musical Experience Questionnaire.

* **Women:** 32; experimental group 15 and control group 17.

# YYYInterventions

* **Experimental group:** Mixed active-receptive group music therapy, alternating listening and playing and singing along; 8 × 1-hour sessions, twice a week during 4 weeks.
* **Control group:** Cooking sessions as another pleasant activity in a group setting, including preparing a different recipe during 8 sessions, twice a week, collectively, with roles distributed according to participants' abilities.

* Emotional status assessed as mood with the STAI-A; timeframe not reported, but reference provided.
* Cognition measured with the SIB; an effect “to a lesser extent” was hypothesised.
* Long-term outcomes were assessed 4 weeks after the last session.

characteristics_risk_of_bias.S:
| Bias domain | Authors’ judgement | Support for judgement |
|---|---|---|
| **Random sequence generation (selection bias)** | Low risk | Randomisation was done by using computerised Excel random number generation technique. |
| **Allocation concealment (selection bias)** | Low risk | Randomisation was done by using computerised Excel random number generation technique. |
| **Blinding of participants and personnel (performance bias) — All outcomes** | Unclear risk | It is not possible to blind surgeons to treatment groups. The experience and number of operating surgeons was not reported. |
| **Blinding of outcome assessment (detection bias) — All outcomes** | High risk | It is not possible to blind surgeons to treatment groups. Surgeons assessed some of the subjective outcomes (complications, EBL, functional scores) therefore we judged there to be high risk for detection bias. |
| **Incomplete outcome data (attrition bias) — All outcomes** | Low risk | Attrition due to death were reported, number of patients lost to follow up at each time point were reported with associated cause. |
| **Selective reporting (reporting bias)** | Unclear risk | A pre-published protocol or clinical trials registration was not reported. |
| **Other bias** | Low risk | No other concerning source of bias was identified. |

characteristics_interventions.S:
## General details

* **Surgeon:** Not reported

* **Components:** The prostheses used in all the cases were bipolar protheses manufactured by Greens Surgical Private Ltd. (India)

* **anaesthesia:** Not reported

* **Care protocol:** A closed suction drain of appropriate size was used in cases where operative time exceeded 90 minutes. Simple Bone cement (40 grams) was used in cases where adequate stability of the prosthesis could not be achieved, especially in those with osteoporotic bones and wide medullary canals. Intravenous Cefuroxime 1.5 gram was administered after skin testing in all cases within one hour of surgical incision as prophylactic antibiotics. Patients in both the groups were ambulated in Zimmer frame from the first post-operative day. They were instructed to avoid squatting and cross-legged sitting for at least six weeks. Weight bearing was allowed from post-operative day as patient was mobilised early and no deep venous thrombosis (DVT) prophylaxis was used.

## Intervention group 1 (Lateral)

Hardinge approach

"The lateral approach involved splitting the Gluteus Medius muscle and retracting one-third of it anteriorly to expose the anterior hip joint capsule."

## Intervention group 2 (Posterior)

Moore approach

"The lateral approach involved splitting the Gluteus Medius muscle and retracting one-third of it anteriorly to expose the anterior hip joint capsule. blunt dissection, after which the pyriformis and short external rotators were detached close to their insertion and reflected back, laying over the sciatic nerve to protect it during the rest of the procedure. In both the approaches, capsulotomy was done with an inverted T-shaped incision, which was repaired in each case after reduction of the prosthesis. The short external rotators and pyriformis were repaired in case of the posterior approach."

"The lateral approach involved splitting the Gluteus Medius muscle and retracting one-third of it anteriorly to expose the anterior hip joint capsule. blunt dissection, after which the pyriformis and short external rotators were detached close to their insertion and reflected back, laying over the sciatic nerve to protect it during the rest of the procedure. In both the approaches, capsulotomy was done with an inverted T-shaped incision, which was repaired in each case after reduction of the prosthesis. The short external rotators and pyriformis were repaired in case of the posterior approach."

Comment: no information was given about the method of allocation sequence.                                                                                                |
| **Deviations from intended interventions** | Low risk of bias   | Comment: the experimental group was treated with silibinin capsule and comparator was administered glucurolactone tablet and inosine tablet, which implies participants, carers, and people delivering the interventions were aware of assigned intervention; all patients completed the trial; analysis was based on intention-to-treat. |
| **Missing outcome data**                   | Low risk of bias   | Comment: according to the results, data were available for all participants.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| **Measurement of the outcome**             | Low risk of bias   | Comment: it is unlikely that the method used to measure non-serious adverse events was inappropriate or differed between groups; outcome assessors were aware of intervention received, but it is unlikely that non-serious adverse events could be influenced by that knowledge.                                                         |
| **Selection of the reported result**       | Some concerns      | Quote: “outcomes were reported at post-treatment 3 months”. Comment: no information was given about pre-specified analysis.                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

characteristics_risk_of_bias.S:
| Bias domain                                                      | Authors’ judgement | Support for judgement                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Random sequence generation (selection bias)**                  | Unclear risk       | “Hospital sites were stratified by unit policy for vaccination, then randomised for their HCWs to be routinely offered either influenza vaccination and their patients unvaccinated (S0P0), staff vaccinated and patients unvaccinated (SVP0), staff unvaccinated and patients vaccinated (S0PV) and both staff and patients vaccinated (SVPV).” *(N.B. the phrase “either influenza vaccination and their patients unvaccinated (S0P0)” is an error and should read: “neither staff nor patients vaccinated (S0P0)”.)*                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **Allocation concealment (selection bias)**                      | Unclear risk       | Not stated.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **Blinding (performance bias and detection bias): All outcomes** | Unclear risk       | Not stated.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **Incomplete outcome data (attrition bias): All outcomes**       | High risk          | Only 654 (61%) of the 1078 HCWs agreed to participate and receive influenza vaccination and 478 (88.8%) of the 538 patients in the “routine vaccination of patients” arms. Serologically proven influenza was ascertained in paired sera in only 225 consenting patients in the “patients not vaccinated” arms.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| **Selective reporting (reporting bias)**                         | Low risk           | No selective reporting.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **Other bias**                                                   | High risk          | Selection bias: the total number of long-term care hospitals in West and Central Scotland is not stated. There were inconsistencies in outcome gradients. In the population under observation, Potter 1997 reported 216 cases of suspected viral illness, 64 cases of ILI, 55 cases of pneumonia, 72 deaths from pneumonia and 148 deaths from all causes; in the sub-population of both vaccinated staff and patients, Potter 1997 reported 24 cases of suspected viral illness, 2 cases of ILI, 7 cases of pneumonia, 10 deaths from pneumonia and 25 deaths from all causes. As these gradients are not plausible, the effect on all-cause mortality is likely to reflect a selection bias rather than a real effect of vaccination. Performance bias: 67% of staff in active arm 1 and 43% in active arm 2 were vaccinated. There is no description of the vaccines administered, vaccine matching or background influenza epidemiology. |

characteristics_markdown.S:
# YYYMethods

| Characteristic                   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Purpose**                      | To assess the effect of staff and patient vaccination against influenza in residents.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **Outcomes named under purpose** | Serologically proven influenza; ILI; lower respiratory tract infection; deaths from all causes; deaths from pneumonia.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **Design**                       | 6 geriatric long-stay hospitals in Glasgow in 1994 had an “opt-out” policy in which patients were routinely given influenza vaccine unless they refused it or had a major contraindication and 6 had an “opt-in” policy in which patients were given vaccine only if they or their relatives requested it following advertisement on the ward that it was available.                                                                                                                                   |
| **Randomisation**                | Hospitals were stratified by policy on vaccination then randomised for their HCWs to be “routinely offered either influenza vaccination or no vaccination.”                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| **Location and period**          | Study conducted in Scotland, during the 1994 to 1995 influenza season, in the community.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| **Follow-up period**             | 1 October 1994 to 31 March 1995.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **Allocation**                   | 12 hospitals were randomly allocated to offer vaccination of HCWs or not; facilities were grouped according to the vaccination policy.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **Vaccination participation**    | The vaccination of staff and patients was voluntary.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **Sub-populations**              | Staff and patients not vaccinated (S0P0); staff not vaccinated, patients vaccinated (S0PV); staff and patients vaccinated (SVPV); staff vaccinated and patients not vaccinated (SVP0).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **Statistical analysis**         | “Baseline characteristics, morbidity and mortality in the 4 groups of hospitals were compared using the X2 test, unpaired Student's test and Wilcoxon rank sum test as appropriate. Odds ratios and 95% CIs were calculated for the effects of staff and patient vaccination. Survival analysis was by Kaplan-Meier product limit estimates, using the Tarone Ware test for statistical significance. Cluster analysis, examining mortality rates and other outcomes by hospital site, was also done.” |

# YYYParticipants

| Characteristic            | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Country**               | Scotland                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **Setting**               | 12 geriatric medical long-term care hospitals in Glasgow                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **Eligible participants** | 1059 hospital residents. All 1078 HCWs (day and night nurses and nursing auxiliaries, ward cleaners, doctors, therapists and porters) in SVPV and SVP0 hospitals were offered vaccination but “voluntary workers, patients' friends and relatives and other casual or occasional ward visitors were not offered vaccine.” Observed units were hospitals and not patients. |
| **HCW participation**     | 654 (61%) of the 1078 agreed to participate; vaccination was contraindicated in 34 (3%) and 47 (4%) were on long-term sick leave and unavailable.                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| **Physical dependency**   | The physical dependency level of patients was measured on the 20-point Barthel scale. The hospitals where patients were routinely offered vaccination (S0PV and SVPV) had lower Bartel scores (P value = 0.003) than those not offered vaccination but there were no differences between hospitals where HCWs were vaccinated and those where they were not.              |
| **Age**                   | 77                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **Gender**                | 71% F                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

# YYYInterventions

Vaccination of patients and HCWs began October 1994 (“4 weeks before the earliest likely start date of the annual influenza outbreak”).

Parenteral influenza vaccine.

Vaccine strains probably matched the circulating strain.

# YYYOutcomes

* Serologically proven influenza (paired sera in 225 consenting patients in the “patients not vaccinated” arms).
* ILI, defined as a temperature of ≥ 37°C, “plus one of the following symptoms: new-onset cough, coryza, sore throat, malaise, headache, or muscle aches,” reported singly or within the ILI outcome and monitored from the end of October 1994 to the end of March 1995.
* LRTI “was identified by the presence of (1) pulmonary crackles, wheeze or tachypnoea plus temp ≥ 37°C or WBC > 10 × 10⁹/L or (2) a positive sputum culture” and was monitored from the end of October 1994 to the end of March 1995.
* Deaths from all causes.
* Deaths from pneumonia.
* All deaths and discharges and admissions to the wards were recorded.
* Ward staff notified the research nurse of any patient who developed clinical symptoms of upper respiratory tract viral illness, influenza or lower respiratory tract infection, and the research nurse visited the patient within 24 hours to record symptoms, clinical signs and investigations on standardised forms.
* “Chest radiographs were not included as part of the routine assessment of suspected lower respiratory tract infection, as for many of the peripheral hospitals, it would have required an ambulance journey for the patient.”
* “Patients with suspected viral illness who gave verbal consent had a nasopharyngeal aspirate (NPA) sample obtained within 48 hours of notification of symptoms. IFA for influenza A and B, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), Chlamydia psittaci and adenovirus antigens” were obtained.
* Antibody levels to *Mycoplasma pneumoniae* were ascertained by complement fixation in consenting patients who had not received influenza vaccination.

# YYYRisk of Bias

| Bias domain                                                      | Authors’ judgement | Support for judgement                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Random sequence generation (selection bias)**                  | Unclear risk       | “Hospital sites were stratified by unit policy for vaccination, then randomised for their HCWs to be routinely offered either influenza vaccination and their patients unvaccinated (S0P0), staff vaccinated and patients unvaccinated (SVP0), staff unvaccinated and patients vaccinated (S0PV) and both staff and patients vaccinated (SVPV).” *(N.B. the phrase “either influenza vaccination and their patients unvaccinated (S0P0)” is an error and should read: “neither staff nor patients vaccinated (S0P0)”.)*                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **Allocation concealment (selection bias)**                      | Unclear risk       | Not stated.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **Blinding (performance bias and detection bias): All outcomes** | Unclear risk       | Not stated.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **Incomplete outcome data (attrition bias): All outcomes**       | High risk          | Only 654 (61%) of the 1078 HCWs agreed to participate and receive influenza vaccination and 478 (88.8%) of the 538 patients in the “routine vaccination of patients” arms. Serologically proven influenza was ascertained in paired sera in only 225 consenting patients in the “patients not vaccinated” arms.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| **Selective reporting (reporting bias)**                         | Low risk           | No selective reporting.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **Other bias**                                                   | High risk          | Selection bias: the total number of long-term care hospitals in West and Central Scotland is not stated. There were inconsistencies in outcome gradients. In the population under observation, Potter 1997 reported 216 cases of suspected viral illness, 64 cases of ILI, 55 cases of pneumonia, 72 deaths from pneumonia and 148 deaths from all causes; in the sub-population of both vaccinated staff and patients, Potter 1997 reported 24 cases of suspected viral illness, 2 cases of ILI, 7 cases of pneumonia, 10 deaths from pneumonia and 25 deaths from all causes. As these gradients are not plausible, the effect on all-cause mortality is likely to reflect a selection bias rather than a real effect of vaccination. Performance bias: 67% of staff in active arm 1 and 43% in active arm 2 were vaccinated. There is no description of the vaccines administered, vaccine matching or background influenza epidemiology. |

characteristics_methods.S:
| Characteristic                   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Purpose**                      | To assess the effect of staff and patient vaccination against influenza in residents.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **Outcomes named under purpose** | Serologically proven influenza; ILI; lower respiratory tract infection; deaths from all causes; deaths from pneumonia.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **Design**                       | 6 geriatric long-stay hospitals in Glasgow in 1994 had an “opt-out” policy in which patients were routinely given influenza vaccine unless they refused it or had a major contraindication and 6 had an “opt-in” policy in which patients were given vaccine only if they or their relatives requested it following advertisement on the ward that it was available.                                                                                                                                   |
| **Randomisation**                | Hospitals were stratified by policy on vaccination then randomised for their HCWs to be “routinely offered either influenza vaccination or no vaccination.”                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| **Location and period**          | Study conducted in Scotland, during the 1994 to 1995 influenza season, in the community.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| **Follow-up period**             | 1 October 1994 to 31 March 1995.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **Allocation**                   | 12 hospitals were randomly allocated to offer vaccination of HCWs or not; facilities were grouped according to the vaccination policy.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **Vaccination participation**    | The vaccination of staff and patients was voluntary.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **Sub-populations**              | Staff and patients not vaccinated (S0P0); staff not vaccinated, patients vaccinated (S0PV); staff and patients vaccinated (SVPV); staff vaccinated and patients not vaccinated (SVP0).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **Statistical analysis**         | “Baseline characteristics, morbidity and mortality in the 4 groups of hospitals were compared using the X2 test, unpaired Student's test and Wilcoxon rank sum test as appropriate. Odds ratios and 95% CIs were calculated for the effects of staff and patient vaccination. Survival analysis was by Kaplan-Meier product limit estimates, using the Tarone Ware test for statistical significance. Cluster analysis, examining mortality rates and other outcomes by hospital site, was also done.” |

characteristics_outcomes.S:
* Serologically proven influenza (paired sera in 225 consenting patients in the “patients not vaccinated” arms).
* ILI, defined as a temperature of ≥ 37°C, “plus one of the following symptoms: new-onset cough, coryza, sore throat, malaise, headache, or muscle aches,” reported singly or within the ILI outcome and monitored from the end of October 1994 to the end of March 1995.
* LRTI “was identified by the presence of (1) pulmonary crackles, wheeze or tachypnoea plus temp ≥ 37°C or WBC > 10 × 10⁹/L or (2) a positive sputum culture” and was monitored from the end of October 1994 to the end of March 1995.
* Deaths from all causes.
* Deaths from pneumonia.
* All deaths and discharges and admissions to the wards were recorded.
* Ward staff notified the research nurse of any patient who developed clinical symptoms of upper respiratory tract viral illness, influenza or lower respiratory tract infection, and the research nurse visited the patient within 24 hours to record symptoms, clinical signs and investigations on standardised forms.
* “Chest radiographs were not included as part of the routine assessment of suspected lower respiratory tract infection, as for many of the peripheral hospitals, it would have required an ambulance journey for the patient.”
* “Patients with suspected viral illness who gave verbal consent had a nasopharyngeal aspirate (NPA) sample obtained within 48 hours of notification of symptoms. IFA for influenza A and B, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), Chlamydia psittaci and adenovirus antigens” were obtained.
* Antibody levels to *Mycoplasma pneumoniae* were ascertained by complement fixation in consenting patients who had not received influenza vaccination.

# YYYMethods

* Study design: parallel-group RCT

* Study centre: single (Special Medical Center of Strategic Support Force, Beijing, China)

* Number randomized: 164 children

* Study follow-up: 12 months

* Exclusions and losses to follow-up: not reported

# YYYParticipants

* Age: mean = 11.5 (SD 2.74) years (range 6 to 16 years)

* Gender: 87 boys, 77 girls

* Culture: Chinese

* Inclusion criteria:

* 6-16 years of age
* binocular myopia and corrected visual acuity 1.0
* capable of language communication, with complete examination and medical history data, and informed consent of family members of children and voluntary participation in study
* Exclusion criteria:

* severe cardiac, hepatic or renal dysfunction
* hereditary myopia, xerophthalmia, acute inflammation of the eye, keratoconus, epilepsy, eye trauma or operation, mental illness or unconsciousness, organic ophthalmopathy
* those who had allergies or contraindications to Atropine drugs or other therapeutic drugs

# YYYInterventions

* 0.01% topical atropine eye drops, one drop, both eyes, before bed, at least 5 times per week (n=82)

Each 1-h class involves a seated warm-up, repetitive and progressive practice of functionally relevant balance and mobility tasks, and a seated cool down. The cool down involves exercises similar to the warm-up but with an emphasis on stretching and relaxation. Instructors are advised to have participants exercise at an intensity of 3–4 (moderate to somewhat hard) on the modifed Borg scale."

Prospective randomised controlled single-centre clinical trial.

Inclusion criteria: Aged between 18 and 70 years; new-onset DVT; the course of disease no longer than 15 days; complete patency of the major branch of the distal iliac vein after CDT with residual stenosis of > 50%; signed informed consent; no contraindications for thrombolytic and anticoagulant therapy.

Exclusion criteria: Patients with severe renal impairment (Cr CL < 30 mL/min); patients in a terminal stage of cancer with a life expectancy of < 3 months, pregnancy, patients with congenital coagulation defects and patients reporting previous or current use of thrombolytic procedures, including surgery and thrombolysis.

# YYYInterventions

Angioplasty or stenting: In the test group, balloon dilatation and stent (diameter: 12–14 mm, length: 6–12 cm) were performed through the lesser saphenous vein, the great saphenous vein, the pretibial vein, or the popliteal vein; residual stenosis < 10% was acceptable.

Control: “The patients in the control group were given the same treatment after the thrombolytic catheters were removed.” No stent was implanted in the control group.

Co-treatment: All participants underwent implantation of an inferior vena cava filter. A 4F Uni*fuse catheter was inserted until the deep vein of affected extremity, including femoro-popliteal segments, through the lesser saphenous vein (n = 46; 69.70%), the great saphenous vein (n = 10; 15.15%), the pretibial vein (n = 5; 7.58%), or the popliteal vein (n = 5; 7.58%); residual stenosis < 10% was acceptable. No participants received intervention by femoral vein access. No further details about puncture, such as ultrasound aid, were given. After discharge from the hospital, participants were advised to wear compression stockings and use oral drugs to promote blood flow (e.g. aescine sodium or diosmin).

Patency of lower extremity deep vein, postoperative clinical efficacy (with VCSS and C in CEAP) and postoperative quality of life (CIVIQ), from baseline until 42 months (follow-up range for all participants, 12–42 months).

Prospective randomised controlled single-centre clinical trial.

characteristics_outcomes.S:
Patency of lower extremity deep vein, postoperative clinical efficacy (with VCSS and C in CEAP) and postoperative quality of life (CIVIQ), from baseline until 42 months (follow-up range for all participants, 12–42 months).

PE and death were not analysed outcomes, but the study authors reported that no fatal PE or death occurred in the study (until 42 months). The study authors related adverse events (two puncture site haemorrhages, one retroperitoneal haemorrhage and three IVC filter thromboses) and recurrence of DVT but did not provide sufficient details for data inclusion in the meta-analysis (e.g. number of events by each group).

Participants: 66 (stenting plus CDT (test group): 27; CDT (control): 39).

Inclusion criteria: Aged between 18 and 70 years; new-onset DVT; the course of disease no longer than 15 days; complete patency of the major branch of the distal iliac vein after CDT with residual stenosis of > 50%; signed informed consent; no contraindications for thrombolytic and anticoagulant therapy.

characteristics_markdown.S:
# YYYMethods

| Characteristic           | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Purpose**              | To assess the effect of staff and resident influenza vaccination on resident all-cause mortality.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **Design**               | C-RCT. A written invitation was sent to the 376 nursing homes with 50 to 200 elderly people (out of a total 1105 nursing homes) in the Paris area and 88 responded. Of these, 40 with staff influenza coverage < 40% during the 2005 to 2006 winter season were selected.                                                                     |
| **Matching**             | Each institution was pair-matched on size, staff vaccination coverage 2005 to 2006 and Group Iso Resources (GIR) weighted average disability score, which ranges from 1 = severe disability to 6 = total autonomy.                                                                                                                            |
| **Randomisation**        | Randomisation was centrally based using a random number generator.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| **Power assumptions**    | It was assumed that the influenza epidemic would last 2 months, mortality would be 8% in the control arm and resident mortality would be reduced 40% after staff vaccination to 4.8% in the intervention arm. 20 pairs of nursing homes with 2000 residents in each group were required to obtain 80% power with 2-tailed hypothesis testing. |
| **Analysis**             | Analysis was by intention-to-treat.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| **Statistical analysis** | “Odds ratios were calculated using alternating logistic regression, with one-nested log odds ratios to model the association between the responses of the same pair and the same nursing home within the pair.”                                                                                                                               |
| **Secondary analysis**   | “In secondary analyses, multivariate estimates were adjusted for the residents' age, vaccination status, GIR disability score and Charlson comorbidity index.”                                                                                                                                                                                |

# YYYParticipants

| Characteristic            | Description                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Country**               | France                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **Setting**               | 40 nursing homes near Paris                                                                                                                                              |
| **Eligible participants** | 3483 patients in the 40 nursing homes                                                                                                                                    |
| **Intervention arm**      | 1592 residents at the beginning and 130 entered the homes during the study period (total = 1722); 989 staff were present at recruitment and 678 (68.6%) were vaccinated. |
| **Control arm**           | 1558 residents at the beginning and 120 entered the homes during the study period (total = 1678); there were 1015 staff at recruitment and 323 (31.8%) were vaccinated.  |
| **Resident vaccination**  | 1452 (84.3%) of patients in the intervention and 1385 (82.5%) in the control group were vaccinated during the 2005 to 2006 winter season.                                |
| **Age**                   | 86                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **Gender**                | 77.% F                                                                                                                                                                   |

# YYYInterventions

## Intervention

* Promotional campaign with posters, leaflets and an information meeting with the study team to sensitise staff to the benefits of influenza vaccination for oneself and residents.
* Face-to-face interviews with each member of staff present in nursing homes between 6 November and 15 December 2006.
* The study team met all administrative staff, technicians and caregivers to invite them to participate and those who volunteered were vaccinated at the end of the interview.
* The vaccine was inactivated Influvac (Solvay Pharma Laboratories), with 15 µG of each of:

  * A/Wisconsin/67/2005-like (H3N2)
  * A/New Caledonia/20/99 (H1NH1)
  * B/Malaysia/2506/2004

## Control

Routine information on influenza vaccination.

# YYYOutcomes

## Primary

* All-cause mortality.

## Secondary

* Influenza, measured when clusters of ILI occurred in residents, using the Quick View Influenza Test.
* ILI, “defined as a fever of ≥ 37.8°C and onset of respiratory symptoms or worsening of chronic respiratory conditions.”
* Proportion of staff who reported ≥ 1 day of sick leave.

characteristics_markdown.S:
# YYYMethods

* Randomised controlled single-centre, open-label, non-inferiority trial.
* Participants randomised in a 1:1 ratio to receive IVM or IVF treatment on day 2 or 3 of the menstrual cycle according to a computer-generated randomisation list.
* Block randomisation was used with a variable block size of 4 or 6.
* Opaque sealed envelopes with randomised assigned groups printed inside were numbered consecutively.
* The randomisation list and envelopes were prepared by a statistician independent of the investigator team.
* Study period: 16 March 2018 to July 2019.
* Study centre, country: Reproductive Medical Center of Peking University Third Hospital, Beijing, China.

# YYYParticipants

* Inclusion criteria: infertile women aged 20–38 years with PCOS as per the revised Rotterdam criteria and without previous IVF attempts.
* Exclusion criteria: women scheduled for preimplantation genetic testing with abnormal results on parental karyotyping; women with congenital or acquired uterine malformations, a history of unilateral ovariectomy, or a male partner with diagnosed azoospermia.
* After assessment for eligibility, 351 were finally enrolled and randomised; 175 to IVM; 176 to conventional IVF.

# YYYInterventions

1 cycle of IVM without the use of gonadotropins or hCG priming versus 1 cycle of standard IVF with ovarian stimulation using a recombinant FSH and GnRH antagonist protocol with recombinant hCG for triggering the ovulation.

In the IVM group, all the COCs were transferred for 28–32 hours into an IVM medium containing 5 mg/mL serum protein substitute in a 5% carbon dioxide incubator at 37 °C. It was supplemented with 75 IU follicle-stimulating hormone and 10 IU hCG. The final concentrations of follicle-stimulating hormone and hCG in the IVM culture system were 0.075 IU/mL and 0.010 IU/mL, respectively. All MII oocytes were inseminated using ICSI.

In the IVF group, fertilisation was achieved by IVF or ICSI as per the seminal analysis.

In both groups, a single blastocyst was transferred and a freeze-all strategy via vitrification was employed.

# YYYOutcomes

* Primary outcome: live birth, defined as a baby born alive after 22 weeks of gestation within 6 months of the first oocyte retrieval after randomisation. The 6-month interval was used to ensure that all women received their first frozen embryo.
* Secondary outcomes: miscarriage (i.e. spontaneous pregnancy loss before 28 weeks of completed gestation), clinical pregnancy (ultrasonic presence of a gestational sac or definitive clinical signs of pregnancy at 7 weeks of gestation), (moderate or severe) OHSS (classified as per the Guideline of the Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists according to the degree of abdominal distention, ovarian enlargement, respiratory haemodynamics and metabolic complications), preterm birth (i.e. birth of a fetus between 28 and 37 weeks of gestation), and congenital anomalies (any structural or functional disorders occurring during the intrauterine life and that can be identified antenatally, at birth, or later in life).

# YYYRisk of Bias

| Bias domain                                            | Authors’ judgement |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------ |
| **Bias arising from the randomisation process**        | Low risk of bias   |
| **Bias due to deviations from intended interventions** | Low risk of bias   |
| **Bias due to missing outcome data**                   | Low risk of bias   |
| **Bias in measurement of the outcome**                 | Low risk of bias   |
| **Bias in selection of the reported result**           | Low risk of bias   |
| **Overall bias**                                       | Low risk of bias   |

The review authors assessed the two new studies at low risk of bias in all five domains and for all outcomes of live birth, miscarriage per clinical pregnancy, clinical pregnancy, OHSS, preterm birth, and congenital anomaly.

# YYYMethods

Study design : parallel RCT. Total study duration : two years (participant enrolment). Details of any 'run in' period : not reported. Number of study centres and location : single-centre: King George’s Medical University, India. Date of study : September 2013 – August 2015 (participant enrolment).

Notes : target sample size was 80 participants.

# YYYParticipants

Number randomised : 61 (surgical management: 34; medical management: 27). Number lost to follow-up : none. Number missing (exclusions & withdrawals) : none. Number analysed : 61 (surgical management: 34; medical management: 27). Number of cross-overs : not reported.

Baseline characteristics : mean age 54.8 years (SD 5.7), male sex 61%, mean GCS score 6.8 (SD 2.3), mean ICH volume 64.6 mL (SD 18.0). ICH location: 15% lobar, 85% deep. IVH extension 51%. No baseline imbalances between the surgical and standard medical management group, besides a more frequent prevalence of hypertension in the surgical group (67.6% vs. 40.7%, p=0.036).

Inclusion criteria :

* Spontaneous supratentorial ICH.

* Age between 20–65 years.

* ICH volume on CT >30 mL.

* GCS score of 4–14.

* The symptoms appearing <72 hours prior to the diagnostic CT scan (an unknown time of symptom onset is exclusionary).

* Negative pregnancy test.

Exclusion criteria :

* Infratentorial extension of haemorrhage.

* Presence of coagulation disorders.

* Pregnancy or lactating females.

* Intra-tumoral haemorrhage.

* CT scan suspicion of haemorrhage due to cerebral aneurysm, AVM, or other vascular anomalies.

* Any concurrent serious illness that would interfere with the safety of the surgery.

# YYYInterventions

Surgical group : craniotomy with haematoma evacuation. The surgical management included a craniotomy, middle frontal gyrus approach, haematoma evacuation, and achievement of haemostasis. No thrombolytic agents were used in any of the patients. EVD was inserted if ventricles were exposed during the surgery, which was removed in 2–3 days or when CSF became clear. Average time from symptom onset to surgery not reported.

Standard medical management group : airway management, O2 by mask or ventilator support, head end elevation by 30°, hydration with input-output charting, control of blood pressure, reduction of ICP using mannitol and furosemide, prophylactic antiepileptic therapy to prevent seizures, prophylactic antibiotics, appropriate feeding, physiotherapy, and management of any associated morbidity, if present. All the patients were kept in the ICU with close monitoring of vital parameters and blood coagulation profile by a team consisting of neurosurgeons, neurophysicians, and critical care experts.

Concomitant interventions : none.

# YYYOutcomes

Primary outcome : mortality at 3 months. Secondary outcome : dependency assessed with the mRS at 3 months (“good functional outcome” defined as mRS ≤3).
